questions: Did s-bend off-track exits fall from 9 of 20 at wheel_track 0.12, and did max_error stay below 0.047?
Did s-bend control_effort fall from 12.2, which would show the narrower track is giving steering authority without extra error?
Did steering_oscillation stay below about 0.4 on the oval and s-bend? If not, is the narrower track adding yaw gain that needs kd or kp retuned?
Did the oval finish rate stay at 1.0?
Did slalom line_loss_events fall below 1.35, or is slalom still 0/20 with line loss near 1.0 at this geometry?

intent: Change one variable from the best design (iteration 5, y 0.08, wheel_track 0.12): reduce wheel_track to 0.10 m. This gives more yaw per PWM difference, so the robot turns more sharply for the same steering signal. All sensor positions, footprints, span, body, wheel radius and mass stay as in iteration 5. Expected: s-bend off-track exits and max_error fall, s-bend control_effort falls, oval finish stays at or near 1.0, and steering_oscillation stays below about 0.4.
learning: Iteration 5 confirmed that lookahead gain continues to y 0.08 (561.6). Iteration 6 tests wheel_track 0.10 at the same lookahead. The sign of the track effect is now set by the contract's turn-rate equation, not by the earlier R2A-era advice.
rationale: Iteration 5 (sensor y 0.08) is the best design so far at 561.6, up from 534.0 at y 0.07 and 454.6 at y 0.06. The lookahead gain has been monotone across y 0.04 (131.9), 0.06 (454.6), 0.07 (534.0) and 0.08 (561.6), and oscillation stayed low (oval 0.20, s-bend 0.32). Oval finish held at 20/20. The s-bend is still the main loss: 9 of 20 runs leave the track, with control_effort 12.2, the highest of any track, so the robot is still working hard in bends. Slalom remains 0/20 with line_loss about 1.35, so no lookahead change is likely to fix it. y 0.08 is the top of the allowed range, so lookahead cannot move further. The next lever is wheel_track. The contract defines turn rate as the wheel speed difference divided by wheel_track, and the PWM difference is set by turn times 350. A narrower track therefore gives more yaw per unit of steering command. This corrects the earlier R2A-era concern that a wider track gives more authority, which was physically backwards. I am keeping every sensor at y 0.08 and all other geometry fixed, and changing only wheel_track from 0.12 to 0.10. The Integrator's gate is met: s-bend off-track exits fell and max_error dropped below 0.048, with oscillation under 0.4. Expected result: s-bend control_effort falls and off-track exits drop below 9 of 20, with the oval staying near 1.0. Risk: the higher yaw gain could raise steering_oscillation; if it rises above about 0.4 or the oval finish falls below 0.85, revert to wheel_track 0.12 at y 0.08, which is the best known design.
